newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fall in PNG Kutubu crude output to reverse in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Fall in PNG Kutubu crude output to reverse in 1998.

text.p: Output from Papua New Guinea's (PNG) Kutubu crude project has declined almost a third this year, industry sources said on Tuesday.
But the decline is expected to be temporary.
New fields scheduled to come onstream by the first quarter of next year should reverse the decline in output, the sources said.
The Kutubu crude field is currently producing 74,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), compared with around 102,000 bpd in January.
"It's a natural decline", said a source at Chevron Corp, who is the operator of the field.
"We have managed to maintain production at more than 100,000 bpd for the past two years through infill drilling, but you can only squeeze so much oil," he said
"We've already recovered two-thirds of the field's reserve, and we recognise that this was going to be the year when we see a sharp decline in output," he added.
Production is expected to hover around 70,000-bpd for the rest of 1997, other sources said.
But Papua New Guinea's new Gobe and Moran fields, which are adjacent to the Kutubu field, are expected to start production by the first quarter of next year.
Crude from Moran and Gobe will be blended to the existing Kutubu production, which should boost output to 100,000 barrels-per-day.
"Production will remain around 100,000 bpd for two to three years," said another Chevron source.
The sources said the blending of the two new crudes would not alter the assay of Kutubu to any great extent.

Kutubu participants are Oil Search with 7.763 percent, Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd with 19.375 percent, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd with 9.688 percent, BP Australia Ltd with 19.3785 percent, Ampolex with 16.455 percent, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd with 4.844 percent and the PNG government with 22.50 percent.
